square.en: Tahrir Square, right in the heart of Cairo, became the epicentre of the uprising.
square.zh: 解放广场（Tahrir Square），位于开罗的正中心，成为了起义的震中。

square.en: Day and night, people occupied the square, camping out despite the threat of violence.
square.zh: 日以继夜，人们占领了广场，不顾暴力威胁在那里露营。

square.en: On the one side, Warsaw had lots of reconstructed churches and historical squares and streets.
square.zh: 一方面，华沙拥有大量重建的教堂、历史广场和街道。

square.en: It has a total land area of 7.7 million square kilometers, about that number.
square.zh: 它的总陆地面积约为 770 万平方公里。

square.en: It still stands in the center of Mexico City, in its main square.
square.zh: 它依然屹立在墨西哥城市中心的宪法广场上。

squeeze.en: It’s expensive to sponsor someone. So students are being squeezed from both sides.
squeeze.zh: 赞助某人成本很高。所以学生们正面临来自双方面的挤压。

squeeze.en: HENRY, all in capital letters, stands for “high earner, not rich yet”, which is used to describe someone who earns a lot of money but still feels financially squeezed.
squeeze.zh: HENRY 全部大写，是“high earner, not rich yet”(高收入但还没富起来)的缩写，用来形容那些收入很高、但依然感觉手头紧的人。

squeeze.en: And they often did. Pick up any Charles Dickens novel and you’ll find depictions of evil employers squeezing their workers for every last penny, paying them the absolute minimum possible for them to not die of starvation or from freezing to death at home.
squeeze.zh: 他们也经常这么做。随便翻开一本 Charles Dickens 的小说，你都能看到对邪恶雇主的描写，他们榨干工人的每一分钱，只支付给他们勉强维持生命、不至于饿死或冻死在家里的最低报酬。

squash.en: Farmers cultivated crops like maize (which is corn), beans, squash, and chili peppers.
squash.zh: 农民种植了诸如玉米（也就是玉米）、豆类、南瓜和辣椒等农作物。

squash.en: In the eastern forests, some farmed crops like corn or beans and squash, and they also hunted and traded.
squash.zh: 在东部森林里，一些人种植玉米、豆类或南瓜等农作物，他们也进行狩猎和贸易。
